emergence.summary: A single-gene SOD1 TOXIC gain-of-function form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: dominant SOD1 variants (e.g. Ala5Val / A4V, Gly94Ala / G93A, Asp91Ala / D90A) do NOT act mainly by losing dismutase activity but by conferring a toxic misfolding/aggregation GAIN that progressively kills motor neurons, suppressing motor-neuron survival and function -> progressive paralysis (the motor-neuron-function axis is driven DOWN). Read with the proteinopathy framing already used for Huntington (HTT) and transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR): the toxic GAIN is an over-active pathological BRAKE on motor-neuron function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), and the kit re-derives the approved therapy, which REMOVES the toxic species rather than treating symptoms -- tofersen, a SOD1 antisense oligonucleotide that lowers SOD1 mRNA/protein (FDA 2023 accelerated approval; the first genetically targeted ALS therapy). This extends the toxic-aggregate 'reduce the poison' pattern (HTT, TTR) onto MOTOR NEURONS, and sits as the toxic-GOF contrast to spinal muscular atrophy's structural-LOF on the SAME cell type (SMA: restore the missing SMN; SOD1-ALS: remove the toxic SOD1). The gamma read is of the SOD1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease-causing point mutations are coding changes outside the promoter firewall, and their toxicity is a protein-misfolding GAIN, not a transcriptional change. (Most ALS is sporadic and non-SOD1; the commonest familial cause is the C9orf72 repeat expansion -- a separate, non-promoter structural lesion outside this single-gene read. This entry is the SOD1 subtype only.) Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: motor-neuron survival and function (progressively suppressed by toxic misfolded-SOD1 aggregation) -- the motor-neuron toxic-GAIN contrast to SMA's motor-neuron loss-of-function

per_gene.note: SOD1 encodes Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase 1. The ALS-causing variants act predominantly through a TOXIC gain-of-function: the mutant protein misfolds and aggregates, conferring motor-neuron toxicity (mitochondrial, proteostatic, prion-like propagation) rather than by loss of dismutase activity -- read here as an over-active pathological BRAKE that SUPPRESSES motor-neuron survival/function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), the same proteinopathy framing as Huntington and TTR. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the toxic coding lesion's magnitude (firewall). 21q22.11 (OMIM 147450). NCBI official symbol SOD1.
per_gene.src: Rosen 1993 Nature 362:59 (SOD1 mutations in familial ALS); Gurney 1994 Science 264:1772 (toxic-GOF mouse); Bruijn 1998 Science 281:1851 (toxicity independent of dismutase activity)

falsifiers.claim: mutant SOD1 acts as an over-active brake suppressing motor-neuron survival/function (axis DOWN) via a toxic gain, not loss of dismutase activity
falsifiers.falsifier: if reducing SOD1 (removing the toxic protein) WORSENED motor-neuron survival, or if a complete SOD1 dismutase-null with no misfolding caused the same ALS, the toxic-suppressing-brake direction would be refuted
falsifiers.measurable_by: motor-neuron survival / motor function vs SOD1 level under SOD1 lowering; phenotype of dismutase-dead-but-stable vs aggregation-prone alleles

falsifiers.claim: lowering SOD1 (reduce) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if lowering SOD1 failed to slow, or accelerated, motor-neuron loss / ALS progression, the reduce-SOD1 lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: ALS progression (ALSFRS-R / survival / neurofilament) vs SOD1-lowering
